guard: every cell in the operator-literal scanner is graded and its discriminator can still say no, so a hollowed-out probe, or a cell that nothing grades, is reported instead of passing silently
why: This is the first fixture in the corpus naming scripts/check-operator-literals.mjs, so before it the selector reported `0 fixture(s) selected from 430` and `{"shards":[]}` for any diff touching the scanner, and the aggregate passed on the resulting skip. Measured at fe813fe390d3ef47ac54325f48be816ebaa84148, where the corpus held 430 fixtures; this is a DATED HISTORICAL figure and is deliberately not restated at the current corpus size, against controls of 3 selected for packages/core/src/membership-feed.ts and 2 for scripts/mutation-coverage.mjs.

Coverage is over CELLS, and the factory is only a grouping. The scanner builds 65 cells: 51 from 3 factories, where one case per factory genuinely grades every cell it builds, and 14 as INLINE object literals with a measure of their own and no factory at all. The partition is MEASURED rather than asserted: the suite's own census row prints `markers=65 parsed=65 (factory=51 inline=14)` from the AST inventory, and 65 is the scanner's own SELFTEST_SUMMARY_ROW cells=65/65, both re-derived at the head this fixture ships on. Two earlier versions of this sentence were stale: it said 34 cells as 27 + 7, then 61 as 51 + 10. #1614 added four INLINE cells (sentence-final-period-ipv6, sentence-final-period-ipv4, letter-adjacent-address, sentence-final-period-refuses-name) while this branch sat in review, so the total and the inline term both moved while the factory term held at 51. The 10 was stale TWICE OVER, and that is the more serious half: the INLINE_CELLS registry in the suite had also not been updated, and nothing could make that fail, because only the claimed->source direction was enforced while the comment above the array claimed both directions. Four inline cells existed in the scanner, never reached the registry, and the suite stayed green at 173/173. This revision brings the registry to 14 and adds the source->claimed direction with a planted control in each direction, so the next four cells cannot land the same way. An earlier version also enumerated FACTORIES and treated that as the denominator, which is this issue's own defect one level down: two reviewers independently hollowed an inline discriminator (workflow-host-exclusion's planted count, to a constant) and measured it SURVIVING at scanner cells=61/61 exit 0 - a DATED figure, measured at the then-current 61-cell head before #1614 and deliberately not restated here - each with a same-run positive control proving the cell was reached. No factory enumeration, however perfect, can see those 14. So the denominator is now the cell list itself and every cell must be graded, covered by its factory, or named as ungraded with a reason.

The suite kills them by the absence of a failure. It tampers each cell's planted subject so the asserted property is genuinely destroyed, then requires that cell's discriminator FIELD to read 0. A live reader flips; a reader returning a constant cannot, so the tamper stops going red and the suite goes red in its place. The field is read rather than the cell's PASS/FAIL status, because on a POSITIVE cell the destroyed subject fails the primary anyway and would mask a dead secondary: measured, that produced one red row and one green row for the same mutant.

The census is BIDIRECTIONAL and it reads CELLS, both established by review rather than by reasoning. Checking only that everything found is named cannot notice something the reader failed to find: the behaviour-neutral edit `function matchCell(` to `function matchCell (` once removed a factory from the census while the suite still reported unaccounted=0 and a full green, and a declaration-shaped line inside a template literal once stood in for a factory that had been refactored away. Both failures came from reading text rather than structure, and widening a pattern only moves the boundary to the next spelling. The denominator now comes from the `// SELFTEST_CELL <id> START/END` markers, the same reader the tampers key on, which review probed hard: a renamed cell reports `found 0/0`, a reformatted one `occurs 0 time(s)`, and a marker quoted in a comment `found 2/2`. A second independent reader parses the SELFTEST_CELLS array from the AST and the two must agree on the count. Each reader carries its own planted control, because a control on one reader says nothing about another.

Nothing is exempt. An earlier version recorded scanCell as a KNOWN LIMIT that reported no secondary reading. That was wrong, and hollowing its metricCount SURVIVED: the field is simply named for the cell's metric rather than `secondary`. A limitation asserted rather than measured is a gap with a label on it, and the label makes it less likely anyone looks again. Being LISTED is likewise not coverage: the suite knows which field each inline cell reports, and deliberately does not accept that as grading it.

The last three mutations guard the harness rather than the scanner: they blind each census direction and make the positional tamper silently do nothing. Any of them would let every case report a pass it did not earn. This matters more than usual here, because an absence-detector emits the same unaccounted=0 whether it is working or blinded, so it cannot be graded by reading its output.

The reader that DECIDES every kill is graded against SYNTHETIC rows it supplies itself, and three reviewers were needed to get this right. Grading it against real runs cannot work, because both halves of every kill correlate perfectly with run identity: the untampered copy always exits 0 and wants a nonzero, every tampered run exits 2 and wants a zero. Measured, `return "0"` passed the suite at 77/77, and after a nonzero-baseline check was added, `return run.exitCode === 0 ? "1" : "0"` still passed at 90/90 without reading a row. So the control hands the reader ONE run with an exit code that is neither 0 nor 2, carrying four mutually inconsistent field values plus two cases that must return undefined. No constant satisfies 2, 3, 5 and 7 at once, an oracle fails all four, and no value-returning shortcut produces undefined. All six reads print on one line, because the inconsistency is the mechanism and is only visible when the values appear together.

The last mutation guards WHERE EVERY TAMPER RUNS. `guardSafe` and `makeWorkdir` were ungraded, and they are load-bearing: if the guard stops rejecting, `makeWorkdir` returns a path whose URL form differs from the concatenation the scanner's self-execute guard compares against, every spawned copy exits 0 having run NOTHING, and every kill in this suite reads that silence as a pass. Hollowing the guard is a NO-OP on a healthy host, which is why it went ungraded by accident: on an unescaped tmpdir `guardSafe = () => true` changes nothing observable. So the added checks feed the guard both answers directly rather than waiting for a hostile host. Measured at this head: `() => true` gives exit 1 at 174/175 with the rejecting check red BY NAME, which is what this mutation scores. `() => false` is also red at exit 1, but it throws out of makeWorkdir at module load before any check row prints, so it is recorded in the file's docblock and deliberately NOT scored here, because a crash is not a graded reading. The makeWorkdir postcondition check is scored separately: returning `candidate + "/"` from the accepted branch keeps the guard intact (a trailing separator does not change the URL form) but breaks the realpath postcondition, because `realpathSync` normalises the separator away, and measured at this head it reds `makeWorkdir returns a realpath'd directory its own guard accepts` BY NAME at exit 1, 174/175.
